# M1 — iteration_after_audit_1 (phase 5.3)

Read `M1-iteration_after_audit_1-CORRECTIVE_TASK.md` completely; it is the authoritative specification for this single bounded pass. Start a NEW Claude Code session in the existing M1 workspace. Continue IN PLACE from the CURRENT `output/template/` (the accepted M1 5.3 iteration-2 result). Never reset or copy it from `baseline/template/`. Leave `baseline/`, `source/`, `audit/`, candidate identity, and all prior iteration files unchanged.

The independent re-audit found one root-cause class of false negatives: valid XML attributes enclosed in SINGLE quotes are missed by both `.claude/scripts/check-architecture.js` and `.claude/scripts/check-manifests.js`. A forbidden `Domain -> Api` `<ProjectReference Include='...'>` and a `Directory.Packages.props` `<PackageVersion Version='*' Include='...'>` can currently pass as clean. Single-quoted `<PackageReference>` also bypasses inline-Version, deprecated/reserved package and test-framework checks. These are real checker defects, not missing policies.

Repair attribute handling with a bounded, consistent strategy that treats single and double quotes equivalently; also preserve attribute order independence, whitespace/multiline elements, nested `<Version>`, `Include`/`Update` where already supported, and genuine XML comments. Test both **detection** and **non-rejection**: disallowed project edges, inline versions, floating/prerelease central versions, deprecated and reserved packages, and correct allowed dependencies/central versions. Ensure relevant diagnostics actually arise; do not count setup errors as negative-test successes. Confirm behavior through the already wired `PostToolUse` and `PostToolUseFailure` hooks after actual `.csproj` edits and failed commands.

Scope: edit only the two checkers above, plus `.claude/scripts/lib/common.js` if a small shared XML-attribute helper demonstrably prevents duplication, and append an evidence-based section to the existing `output/REFINEMENT_REPORT.md`. Add no permanent files or dependencies. Preserve the M1 minimal-modular architecture, four static capability slots (architecture frame; persistence/testing leaves; optional frontend), frame/leaf ownership and `binds`, all 194 policies + GOV-017/018, flat rules, active worktree routing, command classifier, fail-closed PreToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop state, BOM/UTF-16 behavior, and all unrelated current output files byte-for-byte.

Use ONE finite temporary harness under `output/.work/`. First reproduce the original bypass on the untouched current checkers, then apply the smallest root-cause fix, run the finite positive/negative/equivalence cases, unchanged-feature smoke tests, and ONE cumulative confirmation audit. A concrete regression permits one targeted correction and one confirmation repeat, not an indefinite audit-of-audit cycle. If a blocker remains, record exact failing examples and report `BLOCKED` rather than inventing a PASS or repeatedly retrying.

Record changed-file hashes, test counts/results, unchanged-file identity, policy/capability preservation rationale, and known limits in the existing report. Remove `output/.work/` LAST; final `output/` must contain only `template/` and `REFINEMENT_REPORT.md`. STOP after writing the final evidence and report status. A successful outcome is not merely a cleaner parser: it is a reproduced false negative becoming a meaningful failure, with all existing valid cases still passing.
